fullTextEN: Hello! Today I want to talk about,

fullTextZH: 住在中国的农村是什么体验。
fullTextEN: what it's like to live in rural China.
My home is in rural China.
So today I want to talk about,
5 things I find interesting.

fullTextZH: 第一件我觉得有意思的事情是，
fullTextEN: The first interesting thing is,

fullTextZH: 我记得在我们的村子里，
fullTextEN: I remember in our village,
every family would raise pigs.
Yes, when I was young,

fullTextZH: 我们的村子里没有工作。
fullTextEN: there was no work in our village.
Everyone was a farmer,
everyone had to farm,
and had to grow vegetables.

fullTextZH: 所以我记得每个家庭都养猪。
fullTextEN: So I remember every family raised pigs.
So I said,

fullTextZH: 在这个村子里我们没有工作，
fullTextEN: In this village, we had no work,
so, we had no income.

fullTextZH: 因此，每个家庭都需要养猪。
fullTextEN: Therefore, every family needed to raise pigs.

fullTextZH: 对，猪就是我们唯一的收入。
fullTextEN: Yes, pigs were our only income.
No other income, only pigs.

fullTextZH: 当然，现在很多很多的年轻人，
fullTextEN: Of course, nowadays many, many young people,
they go to big cities to work,
go to big cities to work.

fullTextZH: 但是我记得我小的时候，
fullTextEN: But I remember when I was little,

fullTextZH: 我的爸爸妈妈，他们没有工作，
fullTextEN: my parents, they didn't have jobs,
they farmed,
grew vegetables, and they raised pigs.
I also remember when I was little,
if I needed to pay tuition,

fullTextZH: 那我的爸爸妈妈会杀一只猪，
fullTextEN: then my parents would kill a pig,
and then pay my tuition.

fullTextZH: 对，所以如果你看中国的汉字“家”，
fullTextEN: Right, so if you look at the Chinese character '家',
'家' is a roof,
and underneath there is a pig.
Why?
There is a pig at home.
Now that you've heard my story,
maybe you understand,

fullTextZH: 为什么每个人的“家”下面有一只猪。
fullTextEN: why everyone has a pig under their 'home'.

fullTextZH: 因为在中国的农村，真的很多人养猪。
fullTextEN: Because in rural China, many people really raise pigs.
Okay, this is the first thing,
every family raises pigs.
The second thing,

fullTextZH: 我小时候，我也常常爬山，对。
fullTextEN: When I was young, I often climbed mountains, right.
Climbing mountains.

fullTextZH: 可是，我爬山和澳大利亚人爬山不一样。
fullTextEN: But, my mountain climbing is different from Australians'.

fullTextZH: 我小时候爬山，一定是为了吃。
fullTextEN: When I was young, climbing mountains was definitely for eating.
Yes, on the mountains when I was young,

fullTextZH: 有很多很多可以吃的东西。
fullTextEN: there were many things to eat.
There were bayberries, ah,
nuts, right.
There were many things to eat.

fullTextZH: 所以，我爬山是为了吃野果。
fullTextEN: So, I climbed mountains to eat wild fruits.
Now I am in Australia,
I also often climb mountains.
But,
I am very disappointed,
because there are no wild fruits to eat.
The people I climb with think,

fullTextZH: 山上所有的东西都不可以吃，
fullTextEN: everything on the mountain is not edible,
They are all poisonous.
So I think,

fullTextZH: 小时候在我的家爬山更好玩。
fullTextEN: Climbing mountains at my home when I was young was more fun.
Okay, this is the second thing,

fullTextZH: 就是爬山不是为了锻炼身体，
fullTextEN: It's just that climbing mountains is not for exercise,
it's for eating.
The third thing is,

fullTextZH: 在我住的村子里是没有超市的。
fullTextEN: In the village where I live, there is no supermarket.
There isn't a single supermarket.
I remember when I was young,

fullTextZH: 在我的村子里，我们有两个，
fullTextEN: In my village, we had two,
two very small shops.
We called them 'small shops'.

fullTextZH: 这个小卖部，它们没有很多东西，
fullTextEN: These small shops, they didn't have many things,
No vegetables,
No meat, only maybe,
Um, very few snacks,

fullTextZH: 然后可能有一些做饭用的调味料。
fullTextEN: and maybe some cooking condiments.
Oh, maybe some beer,
but not many things.

fullTextZH: 如果你要买菜，你要买衣服，
fullTextEN: If you want to buy groceries, you want to buy clothes,
then maybe you need to go to the market.

fullTextZH: 赶集就是在更大的地方，
fullTextEN: Going to the market means going to a bigger place,
Generally speaking, there is one every month,
a market day.

fullTextZH: 对，那你可以每个月去一次，
fullTextEN: Right, then you can go once a month,
to buy clothes, buy other things.
So how do we buy meat?
In the village where I live,
there is a person,
he rides a motorcycle,
then he shouts loudly, he says:
"Selling pork!"
"Pork! Pork! Pork!"
Then you hear it,

fullTextZH: 你可以大叫，你说：“等一下！
fullTextEN: you can shout, you say: "Wait a moment!
I want to buy pork!"

fullTextZH: 对，所以在我住的村子里，
fullTextEN: Right, so in the village where I live,

fullTextZH: 没有很多可以吃的东西，
fullTextEN: there aren't many things to eat,
nor much entertainment.
As for the fourth one, I want to talk about it,
In the village where I live,
Generally speaking, there's no entertainment.
No KTV, uh,
No badminton,
There's nothing at all.
But during the Spring Festival,

fullTextZH: 我们会请很多人来唱戏。
fullTextEN: we invite many people to perform opera.
Yes, perform opera.

fullTextZH: 其实中国人可能也听不懂，
fullTextEN: Actually, even Chinese people might not understand,
what the opera is about.

fullTextZH: 所以，如果你去我的村子，
fullTextEN: So, if you go to my village,
you will find,
the people on stage are performing opera,

fullTextZH: 可是台下没有什么人看。
fullTextEN: but there aren't many people watching from below.
Because we don't understand it,
we think it's not good to watch.
But, because someone is performing opera,
we feel, ah,
it's very lively, very lively.
So, in my village,
Every year, someone comes to perform opera,
although no one watches.

fullTextZH: 好，那第五个我觉得有意思的事情是，
fullTextEN: Okay, the fifth thing I find interesting is,
I went,
when I went to middle school,
the middle school was not in the countryside,
it was in a town.

fullTextZH: 所以呢，我需要自己背米，
fullTextEN: So, I needed to carry rice myself,
to school.

fullTextZH: 对，每个人都要带米去学校。
fullTextEN: Yes, everyone had to bring rice to school.

fullTextZH: 因为我们要在学校住一个星期，
fullTextEN: Because we had to stay at school for a week,
so we needed to eat.

fullTextZH: 所以呢，每个人都要带米，
fullTextEN: So, everyone had to bring rice,
everyone had to bring their own rice.

fullTextZH: 然后我记得，大部分的人也要自己带菜。
fullTextEN: Then I remember, most people also had to bring their own vegetables.

fullTextZH: 因为那个时候，很多很多人没有钱，
fullTextEN: Because at that time, many people had no money,

fullTextZH: 所以他们没有钱去食堂买菜。
fullTextEN: so they had no money to buy food in the cafeteria.
At my school,
we certainly didn't have a refrigerator.
So, if you brought vegetables,
they might spoil quickly.

fullTextZH: 那很多人，他们带了很咸、很咸、很咸的咸菜，
fullTextEN: Then many people, they brought very salty, very salty, very salty pickles,
or sauerkraut.
So, now I think, um,
at that time,

fullTextZH: 很多很多人的营养可能都不够。
fullTextEN: many people's nutrition might not have been enough.

fullTextZH: 好，这就是我住在中国的农村的体验。
fullTextEN: Okay, this is my experience living in rural China.

fullTextZH: 我觉得现在可能变好了很多很多。
fullTextEN: I think now it might have improved a lot.

fullTextZH: 现在，中国农村的生活可能不一样。
fullTextEN: Now, life in rural China might be different.
But, when I was young,

fullTextZH: 我记得我们的生活就是很简单，
fullTextEN: I remember our life was very simple,
no entertainment,
not many snacks, um.
A little bit boring,
but there were also very happy times.
How about you?

fullTextZH: 你住在一个农村，还是一个大城市？
fullTextEN: Do you live in a rural area or a big city?

fullTextZH: 你觉得住在大城市更好，
fullTextEN: Do you think living in a big city is better,
or is living in the countryside better?
Leave a message and tell me.
Okay, see you next time, bye!
